chunks: And Yūnus narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him: A man stole from the war spoils an amount for which cutting off the hand would become obligatory.

He عليه السلام said: It is to be considered how much his share is. If what he took was less than his portion, he is to be disciplined and the remainder of his property is to be given to him. If he took the like of what belonged to him, then there is nothing upon him. And if he took an excess equal to the price of a shield, and that is a quarter of a dīnār, his hand is cut off.

key_terms.الْقَطْعُ: the hadd punishment of cutting off the hand for qualifying theft
key_terms.الْمَغْنَمِ: war spoils from which eligible participants receive a share
key_terms.رُبُعُ دِينَارٍ: a quarter of a dīnār, the stated value threshold in this report
key_terms.عُزِّرَ: he is subjected to ta'zir, a discretionary disciplinary punishment
key_terms.فَضْلًا: an excess amount beyond what is rightfully his
key_terms.مِجَنٍّ: a shield, used here as a measure for the theft threshold
key_terms.نَصِيبِهِ: his rightful allotted share from the spoils

ai.seo_question: When is the hadd punishment applied for stealing from war spoils if the thief already has a share in them?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding theft from war spoils by someone who has an existing share in them. The ruling depends on comparing what he took with his rightful portion: less than his share entails ta'zir, exactly his share entails no punishment, and excess reaching the theft threshold entails amputation.
